subject: Hack for continuous time to detection

messages.author: 04bc1253505cb1fa
messages.subject: Hack for continuous time to detection
parts:
Attached is R Code for another demonstration of a customized unmarked function (i.e., hack).   In this case, I have altered the "occu" function two do two things:

1) accept single visit, continuous time to detection data
2) use a complementary log-log link for occupancy, so that abundance can be derived.

This model is useful if, instead of repeat visits, you visit each plot once for a longer period of time and record the time when you first detected the species.  It could also be useful for camera trap data, which are really from continuous sensors.  But maybe that bears further discussion.  I tested this model against a Bayesian version from the AHM book (p. 615-617) and got the same results with both methods.  But if you can find bugs or errors let me know.

I have attached an R Script containing a bunch of unmarked functions that you have to run locally, first, to make the occu.cttd function work.  The R code includes the data simulator, and a comparison of the analytical results to the simulation values.

messages.subject: Re: Hack for continuous time to detection
parts:
This is very interesting. Please see my post below in which I have asked about the logic of switching site for time in time to detection scenario. Any ideas about this? i.e. instead of sampling x sites for a period y days. You sample one site over y days within several replicated time/sampling periods. We have camera data looking for foxes at rock wallaby colonies and are interested in the predation risk (how often a fox is present). The data is continuous. I propose sequential sampling periods of 10 days repeated 5 times. So we get ttfd within each 10 day period. (in reality this is probably too short a time given the encounter rate but you get the idea). There could be an issue with autocorrelation between sampling blocks within the sampling period I guess? You would be assuming detection is equal within and between blocks. 

Graeme
